human_substantive_critiques.issue: Confounding of hatchery size-grading/feeding regime with higher stocking density/biomass in the single pooled tank housing the large-sized graded group.
Omission of sample sizes and statistical test names in the Abstract, geographical coordinates of the hatchery facility, and exact MS-222 euthanasia concentration.

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe tank pseudoreplication: treating n1=615 and n2=556 individual fish as independent replicates instead of rearing tanks (only 3 control and 3 graded tanks, with n=1 unreplicated tank for the large graded group) and ad hoc mean-centering of tanks prior to pooling.

Mathematically impossible Fligner-Killeen test statistic for two-group family means (chi-squared = 40.51, P = 0.076 for n1=15, n2=15; at df=1, chi-squared = 40.51 yields P = 1.96e-10, whereas P = 0.076 corresponds to df = 29, proving a 30-group/continuous-vector coding error in R fligner.test).

Swapped Control and Graded Coefficient of Variation (CV) values in the Discussion ('CV = 7.98 and 8.97, and among families = 3.34 and 4.16 for control and graded, respectively', contradicting the Results and Abstract).

Unexplained 21.9% sample attrition of 329 fish (from 1,500 initial fish across 15 families down to 615 + 556 = 1,171 analyzed fish, plus 1 dropped family out of 16 spawned) despite claiming 'Mortality was negligible.'
Typographical omission of the inequality operator in the small size-class threshold ('small (97 mm FL)' instead of '< 97 mm FL' or '<= 97 mm FL').
human_anomaly_details: Reviewer #1 (Prof. Dr. Muhammad Naeem) demanded that the authors cite 6 unrelated papers by his own group on Pakistani warmwater fish proximate composition and length-weight relationships: 'For instance, O. mykiss is recognized as a nutritionally valuable fish species with high protein content (Naeem et al., 2016)... For example, fish growth may be influenced by a range of factors (Javed et al., 1992; Naeem et al., 2010; Naeem et al., 2011; Yousaf et al., 2011; Ismat et al., 2013).' The authors complied by inserting 5 of these citations [47-51] at Line 143 ('Fish growth can, of course, be influenced by a range of factors [47-51]').

human_substantive_critiques.issue: FACS sorting for THY1/integrin and validation by PLZF (ZBTB16) immunocytochemistry does not isolate pure spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) but captures a heterogeneous mixture of undifferentiated and differentiating spermatogonia plus contaminating testicular somatic cells.

Bulk RNA-seq deconvolution via CIBERSORTx is an indirect approximation that yielded implausibly high SSC purity estimates (99% at PND8, 85% at PND15, 82% in adult) and cannot substitute for single-cell resolution across continuous spermatogonial state transitions.

Imprecise developmental terminology (initially using 'SC' which denotes Sertoli cells rather than 'SPG', conflating fetal/neonatal prospermatogonial stages, and omitting prior ATAC-seq studies on mouse spermatogonia).

ai_only_critical_catches: Systemic experimental protocol confounding between the juvenile (PND8/PND15) and Adult stages across every assay: (a) different FACS surface antibodies used for pups (anti-alpha_v-integrin CD51, clone RMV-7, mislabeled as 'integrin a5' in the Key Resources Table) vs. adults (anti-alpha_6-integrin CD49f, clone GoH3); (b) different RNA-seq library preparation inputs (purified column-extracted heat-fragmented RNA for PND8/PND15 vs. direct lysis of 1,000 intact sorted cells at 85C without RNA extraction for adults); (c) a 5-fold difference in Omni-ATAC cell input (25,000 cells in PND15 vs. 5,000 cells in adults); and (d) different tissue dissociation protocols (trypsin only in pups vs. collagenase IV + trypsin + 30% Percoll gradient in adults).

Misattribution of meiotic/post-meiotic spermatocyte and spermatid contamination in adult FACS sorts as novel intrinsic 'adult SPG up-regulated' biology: the highlighted ciliogenesis/flagellar master regulator Rfx2 and GO terms 'cilium movement', 'sperm flagellum', and 'sperm motility' are canonical pachytene spermatocyte/spermatid markers.
Internal arithmetic error in reported adult DEG counts in the Results ('2483 DEGs between PND15 and adult stage (914 down-regulated and 1579 up-regulated)', where 914 + 1579 = 2493 != 2483).

Unbalanced BAM pooling prior to MACS2 peak calling (merging n=6 PND15 replicates of 25,000 cells each vs. n=5 adult replicates of 5,000 cells each without read downsampling) and omission of the explicit batch factor (B1 vs. B2) from the limma-voom and edgeR design matrices.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: SIDER is restricted to post-marketing package inserts of approved drugs (last updated in 2015), introducing survivorship and risk-benefit bias that limits direct generalizability to preclinical/clinical-stage drug discovery safety attrition.
Potential confounding by genetic support for the drug's primary indication, target pleiotropy (number of associated genetic traits), and sensitivity to the MeSH semantic similarity threshold.
Lack of direction-of-effect concordance analysis (agonist vs. antagonist pharmacology relative to gain/loss-of-function human genetics) and breakdown by drug modality.

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe statistical non-independence in all 2x2 Fisher's exact tests and binomial logistic regressions across the 1,187,298 drug-SE pairs: treating shared-target drug pairs (567 drugs mapped to only 275 target genes, e.g., 40 drugs sharing just 7 target genes for tachycardia) and ontologically correlated MeSH SE terms as independent Bernoulli trials, massively deflating p-values (e.g., P = 7.1e-93).

Methodological contradiction between the Results text (stating drug-SE pairs with Sim(Indication, SE) >= 0.9 were removed from the analysis universe) and the Methods text (stating Sim(Genetic Trait, Indication) < 0.9 was required for a target-indication-SE trio to count as having genetic support, leaving the pair in the non-genetically-supported denominator).
Case-only conditioning (Y = 1) in the SIDER side-effect frequency and placebo-status logistic regression models (glm(sim_assoc ~ frequency)).

Unreplaced template placeholder 'X' in Supporting Information S2 Fig caption ('driven by GWAS associations for X genes: CYP19A1..., ESR1..., FGFR2..., INSR..., and SRD5A2...') and unformatted dangling reference numbers '34,35' in Methods Line 108 where the reference list ends at [26].

human_substantive_critiques.issue: High rejection rate during baseline population calibration (only 11,847 accepted out of 100,000 initial models) and lack of clarity on how 11,847 baseline models expanded into 60,599 drug intervention models.
Strong collinearity between Delta_RMP and Delta_APA (r = -0.88) potentially distorting SHAP feature importance rankings, prompting a request for PCA dimensionality reduction.

Overly simplistic binary classification framing (Class III vs. non-Class III rather than multi-class Vaughan Williams classification or proarrhythmic risk stratification) and limited methodological novelty.

ai_only_critical_catches: Catastrophic data leakage in the ML train/test split: performing a random 70/30 row-wise split across 60,599 simulated (virtual_cell, drug) action potentials generated from only 12 deterministic drug pore-block profiles, so that all 12 drugs and identical baseline virtual cells appear in both training and test sets rather than splitting by drug (leave-one-drug-out).

Direct test-set leakage during hyperparameter tuning: Methods Section 5.6 explicitly states GridSearchCV was used 'to find the combination of hyperparameters that maximizes its AUC on the test data set.'

Mathematically impossible confusion-matrix metrics across Tables 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7 where Accuracy (ACC) is strictly greater than both Sensitivity (SEN) and Specificity (SPE) (e.g., Table 1 Male LR ACC = 0.6553 while SEN = 0.6063 and SPE = 0.6198; Female LR ACC = 0.6707 while SEN = 0.5790 and SPE = 0.6225), forensically proven by F1 = 2*SEN*SPE/(SEN+SPE) to be a Python coding bug that substituted Precision (PPV) into the Specificity (SPE) column across every table.

Exact linear dependence among 3 of the 14 features (Delta_APD_tri = Delta_APD90 - Delta_APD50, Delta_CTD_tri = Delta_CTD90 - Delta_CTD50, Delta_CTA = Delta_CTmax - Delta_CTD), reducing the rank of the 14-feature matrix to 11 so that PCs 12-14 have zero variance and yield identical metrics to 4 decimal places in Table 4, which the authors falsely interpreted as PCA feature reduction improving accuracy.

Copy-pasted irrelevant epidemiological methods in Section 5.8 ('Hazard ratios and corresponding 95% confidence intervals were calculated using conditional logistic regression models') and hallucinated claims in Discussion Section 3.3 asserting that 'in vitro patch-clamp measurements' served as 'the foundational training set for our machine learning models' and that Delta_AREA improved 'classification AUC for drug-induced proarrhythmia by ~2.1%.'

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Need to directly test whether the embryo itself (prior to E12.5 fetal liver formation) possesses any HAAO enzymatic activity by assaying whole E11.5 embryos and E14.5 liver-excised embryos.
Lack of direct spatial/histological validation (in situ hybridization or immunohistochemistry) of scRNA-seq kynurenine pathway gene expression in the yolk sac endoderm.
Distinction between de novo NAD synthesis starting from L-tryptophan (requiring Tdo2, which is absent in mouse yolk sac endoderm) versus from maternal L-kynurenine.
Vague malformation terminology in Table S4 and need for clearer discussion of differential organ susceptibility to NAD deficiency.

ai_only_critical_catches: Analyzing the 2x2 factorial experimental design (Diet NW15 vs. NW3.5 x Genotype Haao+/- vs. Haao-/-, nested within maternal litters) at E10.5 using a 4-group one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post-hoc test instead of a two-way linear mixed-effects model accounting for the Diet x Genotype interaction and litter-level random effects.

Measurement-error and sample-unit mismatch in the E10.5 correlation analyses (Fig 5I-K) caused by pairing pooled yolk sac metabolite measurements (2-3 yolk sacs per pool) against individual embryo NAD+ measurements.

Bioinformatics reference/annotation mismatch in Methods Line 107 stating that human bulk RNA-seq reads were aligned to human reference genome hg38 but quantified against the mouse GENCODE vM10 annotation.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Potential confounding by sex-chromosome linkage (X/Y vs. autosomal transcripts), which carries distinct evolutionary rate expectations under Faster-X or Y-degeneration models.
High redundancy and potential transcript overestimation in the de novo Trinity transcriptome assembly (59,051 unitigs compared to typical diploid cucurbit genome gene counts).
Confusing and poorly supported argument linking codon usage bias (ENC), synonymous substitution rates (dS), and elevated dN/dS in sex-biased genes.

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe methodological asymmetry in orthogroup construction: comparing de novo short-read Trinity RNA-seq assemblies (clustered at 95% identity) for the two focal dioecious species (T. pilosa and T. kirilowii) against reference genome CDS annotations for the two monoecious outgroups (T. anguina and L. cylindrica), which systematically inflates terminal-branch dN, dS, and frameshift/indel alignment artifacts on the focal T. pilosa branch.

Unacknowledged 2.35-fold spike in synonymous substitution rates (dS) in male-biased floral bud genes (median dS = 0.0728 vs. 0.0310 in unbiased genes, Wilcoxon P = 2.2e-16 in Free-Ratio and P = 6.215e-16 in Two-Ratio models, with extreme dS ~ 2.0 outliers), demonstrating that divergence in male-biased orthogroups is heavily driven by paralogous/allelic mis-assembly rather than positive selection on dN alone.

Misinterpretation of the HyPhy RELAX selection intensity parameter K > 1 (which tests for intensification of overall selection affecting both purifying omega < 1 and positive omega > 1 regimes) as a standalone test of 'positive selection', resulting in near-zero concordance with PAML Branch-Site Model A (only 1 overlapping gene between 98 Branch-Site and 39 RELAX candidates).

10-fold arithmetic error in the reported percentage of sex-linked male-biased genes in Discussion Line 141 ('3/343 = 0.087%' instead of 0.875%)—which was ironically introduced by Reviewer #3 in peer review and copied verbatim by the authors.

Uncontrolled tissue-composition confounding between multi-flower racemose male buds (containing mature pre-anthesis pollen/anthers) and solitary female buds, and absence of multiple-testing correction across the 18 pairwise tests in Table S7.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Potential selection/survival bias from retrospectively enrolling 50% (8/16) of the focal CD4 <200 group (alongside 8 participants with CD4 >=200) one year after primary vaccination.
Ambiguity regarding whether the primary longitudinal outcome model adjusted for booster doses and breakthrough infections, and differences in booster uptake between groups in Table 1.

Unexplained missing data in Table 1 where category counts for vaccines received (n=403) and infection history do not sum to N=448, and unredeemed claim in Methods that comorbidity data were systematically collected.

ai_only_critical_catches: Transposed 95% confidence intervals between the small CD4 <200 group (n=16) and the large CD4 >=200 group (n=432) throughout the Abstract, Results, and S3 Table: the manuscript reports a narrow 95% CI for n=16 (547 BAU/mL, 95% CI 499-595, half-width 48.0) and a 5.2-fold wider 95% CI for n=432 (1399 BAU/mL, 95% CI 1149-1648, half-width 249.5), where the ratio of half-widths (249.5 / 48.0 = 5.20) exactly matches sqrt(432 / 16) = 5.196, proving that the standard errors/CIs of the two groups were swapped during table transcription (and similarly for the slope CIs [-0.320 to -0.311] vs [-0.181 to -0.143]).

Mathematically impossible point estimate and interval in Table 1 for the CD4 <200 group's time since last COVID-19 vaccination ('65 (188-236)' days, where the median/mean point estimate 65 lies entirely outside the interval 188-236).

Inaccurate Table 1 footnote attributing column-percentage sums != 100% to 'Missing data was rounded to one decimal place', when Missing data is reported only as raw counts in footnotes and excluded from percentage denominators.

Unexplained structural specification change between the primary unadjusted mixed-effects model (which includes quadratic time Time^2) and the secondary multivariable mixed-effects model in Table 2 (which omits Time^2 and forces strictly linear time decay across 24 months of multi-wave booster peaks).
human_anomaly_details: Reviewer #3 provided a 3-sentence generic boilerplate endorsement containing zero substantive or technical critiques: 'Overall, I find this article interesting and valuable. The proposed study addresses an important and novel research question. The writing is easy to understand, and the flow of the text is good; the topic is clinically relevant and has ethics committee approval; there are some spelling and grammar errors that need revision.'

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Confounding from cross-sectional study designs (sampling after disease onset or treatment initiation rather than prospectively prior to diagnosis) and variable antibiotic/insulin exposures.
Overinterpretation of statistically non-significant pooled diversity differences (such as in T1DM and asthma) as 'trends'.
Lack of formal statistical validation for the qualitative clustering heatmap comparing disease-associated bacterial taxa against delivery mode and breastfeeding status.

ai_only_critical_catches: Complete omission of quantitative between-study heterogeneity metrics (I^2, Cochran's Q p-value, and tau^2) across every primary and subgroup meta-analysis in the text, tables, and forest plots, violating PRISMA and Cochrane meta-analysis standards.

Severe small-k variance estimation instability in the metafor random-effects models, exemplified by the T1DM pre/at-diagnosis subgroup analysis (k=5 studies, Fig S4) producing an implausibly wide 95% CI of [-2.35, 2.10] (spanning 4.45 standard deviations) while individual study SMDs are tightly clustered near zero (0.01, -0.02, -0.11, -0.10, -0.74).

Direct internal contradiction in age eligibility criteria: Methods states 'We excluded studies where the microbiome was measured at <1 year of age to limit the impact of rapid changes in the infant gut microbiome', whereas the Results, Discussion, and forest plots heavily rely on infant cohorts sampled at <1 year of age (1 month, 3-6 months, and 1-11 months across eczema, food allergy, and asthma studies).

Unreported mathematical conversion of graphical medians and ranges/IQRs into means and standard deviations (citing Hozo et al. 2005 only in the supplement without sensitivity analysis) and pooling multiple arms from the same study (Chua 2018 a/b/c) without accounting for shared control groups or within-study correlation.

Non-systematic cherry-picking of only 4 comparator papers ([115-118]) outside the PRISMA search to construct the 'C-section' and 'no breastfeeding' reference profiles in the ComplexHeatmap clustering analysis, combined with unadjusted binary vote-counting (+1/-1/0) across studies of vastly different sample sizes.
human_anomaly_details: Both Reviewer #1 and Reviewer #2 exhibit strong hallmarks of LLM-generated peer review reports. Reviewer #1 consists of 10 generic textbook bullet points—including falsely claiming 'Limiting the included studies to English-only publications may introduce language bias' when the manuscript explicitly stated 'without language restrictions'—and Reviewer #2 consists of 5 paragraphs of generic praise ('This manuscript offers an insightful and timely exploration... It’s clear that a lot of thought and effort went into this work...').

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Small sample size (N=24 clones across 12 populations) and single summer sampling timepoint limiting statistical power for environmental association claims.
Potential batch effects from sampling the three common gardens in different years (2017 vs. 2019) confounding cross-site gene expression comparisons.
Missing DDBJ accession numbers ('Reads are under registration process') and unspecified bioinformatics parameters for hisat2, psiclass, and stringtie.
Apparent contradiction in discussing 24 disease-resistance genes in the grey60 module despite no statistically significant GO term enrichment.

ai_only_critical_catches: Post-hoc abandonment of multiple-testing correction: after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the 38 WGCNA modules yielded zero significant associations at two of the three common gardens (MYG and IBR), the authors reverted to an unadjusted nominal p <= 0.001 threshold across ~2,736 module-trait correlation tests.

Severe internal inconsistencies in Table 2: (a) module MEgreenyellow is reported as containing 152 transcripts in the Genetic group section of Table 2 (matching Results Line 224) but 395 transcripts in the PC1_SNP section of the exact same table; and (b) reported Benjamini-Hochberg FDR values in Table 2 violate mathematical monotonicity with respect to raw p-values within the same test family (e.g., at KMT for Genetic group, p = 3.21e-4 has FDR = 0.0122 whereas a larger p = 5.42e-4 has a smaller FDR = 0.0103; in PC1_SNP, p = 2.04e-4 has FDR = 0.0026 whereas p = 9.07e-4 has FDR = 0.0005).

Incompatible correlation coefficient and p-value reported in Results Line 296 for hub transcript CJHT.16203.1 with climatic variable CTD ('r = 0.58, p = 0.0819'), where r = 0.58 at N = 24 yields p = 0.0030, whereas p = 0.0819 is not statistically significant even at nominal alpha = 0.05.

Severe false-positive inflation in the revision-added pcadapt outlier scan on N=24 individuals (flagging 1,277 out of 11,175 LD-pruned SNPs [11.4%] as selection outliers) followed by 1,277 x 21 = 26,817 unadjusted Kruskal-Wallis tests at nominal p < 0.01.

Complete confounding of the yaku-sugi genetic lineage with a single geographic source population (YKS, n=4 clones from one island stand), providing df = 0 at the population level to separate lineage genetics from local climate.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Drastic difference in taxonomic composition between PacBio full-length 16S and Illumina V3-V4 16S amplicon sequencing (~1% vs. ~30% Actinobacteria in watered control roots) requiring primer-bias validation.
Overstatement in claiming that the lack of correlation between single-strain gnotobiotic drought enrichment (DE) and seedling biomass challenges the ecological 'cry for help' framework.
Lack of direct correlation analysis linking untargeted LC-MS/MS exometabolomic molecules to DE or plant growth promotion scores across the strain panel.
Need for expanded description of the genomic neighborhoods surrounding the 8 fabG and proP gene clusters and discussion of plant physiological drought responses beyond biomass.

ai_only_critical_catches: Scale-dependent ad hoc PGLS filtering across 7,737 ortholog gene clusters using raw unstandardized regression slopes and standard errors (slope > 0.25 and SE < 0.25) instead of scale-invariant t-statistics (t = slope / SE) and genome-wide Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q-values, which biases discovery toward high-copy-number gene families with large variance (such as fabG, 6-21 copies) and omits raw/adjusted p-values for the 8 candidate gene families.

Internal discrepancy in the ortholog pre-filtering variance threshold between the Results text (Line 231, stating variance < 0.2 across the 24 genomes was excluded) and the Methods text (Line 508, stating variance < 0.25 was excluded).

Pseudoreplication in the gnotobiotic sorghum seedling mono-association growth assays: treating n=15 individual seedlings pooled across 3 sealed microboxes (5 seedlings sharing root space and inoculum per box) as independent biological replicates in one-way ANOVAs and Dunnett's tests rather than treating the microbox (n=3) as the experimental unit or fitting a mixed model with (1 | box).

Arbitrary constant zero-imputation (0.0001) for undetected negative-control qPCR values and multiplication of all 5 biological replicates within a treatment group by a single group-averaged qPCR copy number prior to running two-sided t-tests for the strain DE scores.
